front: If a chemical reaction has occurred, what sort things might we witness?
back:
Bubbling
Colour change
Temperature change
Precipitate (a solid forming in a solution)

front: What is the test for oxygen gas?
back:
Insert a glowing splint into the boiling tube;
If oxygen is present, the splint will relight.

front: What is the test for carbon dioxide gas?
back:
Bubble it through limewater
It turns from clear to cloudy

front: What is the test for hydrogen gas?
back:
Lit splint near the top of a test tube containing hydrogen.
If hydrogen present, it will produce a “squeaky pop”.

Reaction of a fuel with plenty of oxygen
The maximum amount of energy is given out
Water and carbon dioxide are produced as waste products.

Incomplete combustion happens in limited oxygen.
Water is still produced, but carbon monoxide and carbon (soot) are also produced.
Less energy is released.

Diffusion is the spreading out of particles from a high concentration to a low concentration.
This takes no extra energy (passive).
It only happens in gases and liquids.

front: What direction will the particles move in?
back:
The particles will move from left to right.
They diffuse from an area of high concentration on the left to lower concentration on the right.

front: What numbers relate to acids, alkalis and neutral on the pH scale?
back:
Substances with a pH below 7 are acidic
Substances with a pH above 7 are alkaline
Substances with a pH of 7 are neutral

front: How do you name the salt produced in a neutralisation reaction?
back:
The first word is the metal
The second word comes from the acid:
Hydrochloric acid = chloride
Sulfuric acid = sulfate
Nitric acid = nitrate

front: Explain how an acid can be neutralised.
back:
Add alkali to the acid a bit at a time
Use an indicator to tell when the neutralisation point has been reached.
E.g. universal indicator will turn green
An indicator changes colour when it is added to acidic or alkaline solutions.

front: What colour will universal indicator turn when exposed to acids, alkalis & neutral substances?
back:
Acid - red / orange
Neutral - green
Alkali - blue / purple

What are the different variables in a practical investigation?
back:
Independent variable (IV) - the thing you change.
Dependent variable (DV) - the thing you measure.
Control variables (CV) - the things you keep constant (the same).
